positioning.organization: CyberAlchemy: a research lab exploring intelligence, complex systems and human-machine ergonomics.
positioning.product: CyberAlchemy Lab: an open-source company brain system, the user-approved descriptor.
positioning.audience_hypothesis: Software, research and operations teams coordinating people and agents across work that requires continuing context.
positioning.problem: Reconstructing meanings, evidence, decisions and permissions when work changes hands or sessions.
positioning.value_proposition: Make the knowledge behind work inspectable and recoverable through explicit, connected records.
positioning.familiar_context: Knowledge and work organization; company brain is explained through durable project state, not consciousness.
positioning.alternatives_hypothesis: Scattered conversations, document stores and manual context reconstruction. This is an editorial hypothesis, not customer or competitor research.
mechanisms: explicit record formats and declared connections
positioning.evidence_boundary: Explain the documented model and fictional case. Do not claim measured savings, customer adoption, production integrations, complete implementation or resolved alignment.
positioning.call_to_action: Read Start here, then follow the incident or inspect the system map.

alignment.meaning: The research problem of AI behavior corresponding to human intentions and values, including disagreement, incomplete specifications and changing circumstances.
alignment.connection_to_ambition: Increasing general capability should be accompanied by better means of expressing direction, examining behavior and correcting it.
alignment.lab_contribution_hypothesis: Explicit meanings, bounded permissions, inspectable evidence and persistent corrections provide a setting for empirical alignment questions.
alignment.claim_ceiling: Governance records do not demonstrate model alignment or replace training, behavioral evaluation, adversarial evaluation or oversight.
examples_of_questions: Can bounded permissions and visible evidence improve detection of a bad action?
Can project state preserve corrections across different agent sessions?

editorial_guidelines: Preserve the questions What if? and How to? and the user's deviant, renegade research voice.
Attach each belief to a practice: learn unfamiliar subjects, examine premises, retain counterexamples, welcome correction.
Use cybernetic and alchemical metaphors sparingly and immediately explain the concrete work they refer to.
Introduce the product through a recognizable problem and an intended audience before explaining mechanisms.
Treat positioning as a hypothesis until supported by user and customer research.
Give the reader enough specificity to inspect a claim without repeating the entire reference model.
Use precise distinctions between an observation, an assessment, a proposal, an accepted decision and a permitted effect.
Keep organizational research ambition distinct from implemented capabilities and demonstrated outcomes.
Machine agents are ephemeral; durable memory is project state; short-term memory belongs to the session.
An ontology view organizes declared concepts and connections; it is not automatic truth or authority.
Alignment includes human values and the effects on people; do not reduce it to agent obedience or formal permissions.
Keep sources adjacent to the claims they support. Avoid invented people, publications, deployments, customers or numerical benefits.
Use open editorial rows, internal rules and diagrams that support the reading sequence rather than repeated decorative cards.
The feedback figure and session handoff show an editorial process, not newly admitted ontology relations.
